blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Beyond Mathematics
blocks.content: **General Knowledge** isn't just trivia; it's the fuel for a curious mind. This section tests your awareness of the world: science, history, geography, current affairs, and logic. A well-rounded student doesn't just know formulas; they understand the world those formulas describe. GK questions sharpen your brain and improve your ability to think critically across subjects.

blocks.title: 2. The Strategy: Read Widely, Think Deeply
blocks.content:
GK can't be crammed overnight. Build it gradually:

• Read newspapers or news apps for 10 minutes daily.
• Watch educational videos on science and history.
• Play quiz games with friends.
• Keep a 'fact journal' where you write one interesting thing you learned each day.

blocks.title: 3. The Method: Elimination Strategy
blocks.content:
When faced with a multiple-choice GK question you don't know:

1. Eliminate obviously wrong options first.
2. Look for clues in the question itself.
3. Use logic and common sense.
4. If two options are very similar, the answer is usually one of them.
5. Never leave a question blank. An educated guess is better than nothing.

blocks.title: 4. Key Areas to Focus On
blocks.content:
The most commonly tested GK areas:

• **Science:** Planets, elements, inventions, human body.
• **Geography:** Countries, capitals, rivers, mountains.
• **History:** Major events, famous leaders, dates.
• **Current Affairs:** Recent discoveries, awards, sports.
• **Logic:** Patterns, analogies, odd-one-out.

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The biggest GK trap: overconfidence! Students often rush through GK questions because they 'feel easy'. But the details matter. Confusing Mercury (planet) with Mercury (element), or mixing up 'latitude' and 'longitude' can cost you marks. Read every option carefully before selecting your answer.
